## Key Points

### About the Module

This module teaches you to think like a researcher:

- How do we design studies that can answer our questions?
- How do we analyse data to draw conclusions?
- How do we report findings professionally?

### DataLab: Grow Your Own Psychology Data

Your first lab is **DataLab**—a series of 6 cognitive tasks where you'll generate the dataset used throughout the term. You'll learn statistics using *your own data*.

### The 6 Stations

| Station | Name | What You'll Do |
|---------|------|----------------|
| 1 | **Reflex Test** | Catch a falling ruler to measure reaction time |
| 2 | **Mind Palace** | Memorise words, do maths, then recall |
| 3 | **Time Warp** | Estimate time and physical lengths |
| 4 | **Sixth Sense** | Try to detect when someone is watching you |
| 5 | **Lady Luck** | Generate random numbers, roll dice, flip coins |
| 6 | **Frontal Lob** | Rate your ability then throw at a target |

### The Pre-Post Design

We'll measure your mood twice — before and after the stations — to see if DataLab affects how you feel. This is an example of a within-subjects design.

### Assessments

| Assessment | Weight | When |
|------------|--------|------|
| Research Plan | 20% | Week 16 |
| MCQ Exam | 20% | Week 18 |
| EDS Assignment | 20% | Week 20 |
| Research Report | 40% | 1 May (post-term) |

See the [Assessments](../../assessments.qmd) page for details.

### Project Groups

By the end of Thursday, form groups of 3-4 students. You'll work together for the rest of the term on the group research project.

## Before Your Lab

1. Note your lab allocation (Lab A or Lab B)
2. Arrive on time — Thursday 10:00
3. Bring a phone or laptop to record your data
